top_signals.title: Murphy Oil Draws Boycott Call Over Israeli Gas Licenses
top_signals.summary: Pro-Palestinian activists who pressured Eni and Dana Petroleum to quit an Israeli offshore gas venture are now going after Murphy Oil, the Houston-based company that replaced them on Monday. The Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement and its partners called on Murphy on Wednesday to give up the six Zone G exploration licenses it holds 50-50 with Israel’s Ratio Energies. The licenses cover about 1,700 square kilometers of seabed near the Leviathan gas field, and Murphy is the operator. Israel awarded Zone G in October 2023 to Eni, Ratio…

top_signals.title: H&R’s $4.7 Billion Breakup Faces Revolt by Major Investors
top_signals.summary: H&R Real Estate Investment Trust’s C$6.7 billion ($4.7 billion) breakup is facing a growing shareholder revolt, with some of the world’s biggest pension funds lining up against a deal that would hand a chunk of the Canadian landlord’s properties to the family of its chief executive officer.

top_signals.title: Voters Asking For 'Bold Action' From Democrats, Says Deluzio
top_signals.summary: Democratic Representative Chris Deluzio, who’s on the House Armed Services Committee, said the failed impeachment effort of Pete Hegseth 'shouldn't be the end of the oversight' over the defense secretary. Deluzio, who represents Pennsylvania's 17th District, said that holding the Trump administration accountable is just one part of the 'bold action' voters are asking for when Democrats take control of Congress in the new year.  (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Wall St Races for Megadeals as Countdown Begins on Trump Era
top_signals.summary: Bloomberg’s Ryan Gould joins Dani Burger on “Bloomberg Deals.” President Trump’s return to the White House changed the political calculus around mergers and acquisitions, reviving companies’ desire for dream deals that had become difficult to pull off. Now, corporate America is on the clock. (Source: Bloomberg)
